newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: IMF mission to visit Kazakhstan in April.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to visit Kazakhstan in April.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will send a mission to oil-rich Kazakhstan in the second half of April, a fund official said on Wednesday.
"The next mission visit will be sometime in the third week of April," David Hoelscher, the IMF's resident representative in Kazakhstan, told Reuters.
He said the mission would meet officials in the former Soviet republic to discuss the fund's programme for the rest of this year.

The IMF approved in January the disbursement of part of a $446 million Extended Fund Facility agreed last July after a previous mission of the fund had found that reforms in the Central Asian state were on course.
The government aims to cut annual inflation to 17 percent this year from 28.7 percent in 1996.
Industrial output is targeted to rise this year by two percent, compared to a moderate growth of 0.5 percent in 1996.
